p3a_claim: All 10 pilot files are present in P3A's 02-FILES.jsonl with assigned source IDs S0007/S0013/S0023/S0024/S0025/S0028/S0030/S0033/S0035/S0041.
notes: P3A coverage of this window is complete. No file in the pilot window is unknown to P3A.

p3a_claim: best_historical_date for F0003=2026-07-11, F0009=2026-07-27, F0010=2026-06-26 (basis=EXPLICIT in all three).
new_finding: All three are WRONG. Complete-file reading establishes F0003=2026-08-03, F0009=2026-08-02, F0010=2026-08-02. In each case P3A selected a date that the document CITES rather than the date the document was WRITTEN: F0003's 2026-07-11 is an ARB refinement recorded in table row C-11; F0009's 2026-07-27 is the DA clarification being quoted; F0010's 2026-06-26 is the ADOPTION date of Round47-00, a cited artifact.
disagreement: 3 of 10 files (30%). The error is systematic, not random: P3A appears to take the MINIMUM of explicit_dates, which is biased toward making synthesis documents look older than their own sources — because synthesis documents cite older artifacts by construction.
notes: CONSEQUENCE, verified: P3A's ordering places F0010 FIRST of all ten. But F0010 refutes F0008's F-3 AND lists F0008 under 'Inputs reviewed'. A reconstruction built on P3A dates would therefore invert the correction direction — concluding the refutation preceded the claim it refutes. This is the single most consequential finding of the pilot.

p3a_claim: All 10 files carry mtime_block='BULK-01' and order_evidence='INTERNAL-TIMESTAMP'.
new_finding: P3A had ALREADY detected the bulk-mtime problem and had already decided not to trust the filesystem timestamp — it built an explicit-date extraction layer precisely because of it.
agreement: AGREE — and P3A was ahead of the Master Protocol here
notes: PILOT-F14: the protocol (§3, as amended after the first pilot pass) treats the bulk-mtime discovery as new. It was not: P3A's schema records it per-file. §1 lists P3A as a 'navigation aid' and 'candidate evidence' but the protocol never instructs the worker to CONSULT P3A's file-level metadata before deriving chronology. I rediscovered independently what was already recorded.

p3a_claim: P3A's 1,793 reconciliation pairs are OBJECT-LABEL pairs (a='200-step-longitudinal-verification-programme', b='invariant-consolidation-satisfiability-plan'), not file pairs. 55 pairs touch objects P3A attributes to the 10 pilot files; NONE is a file-to-file edge between any two of them.
new_finding: All 10 verified file edges produced by this pilot (R-0001..R-0010) have NO P3A counterpart — not because P3A rejected them, but because P3A does not model file-to-file relationships at all.
disagreement: Structural, not factual: the two reconstructions answer different questions at different altitudes.
notes: This is §31 (file-level edge != theory-level edge) appearing as a structural difference between two whole methodologies. P3A reconstructs the OBJECT graph; this protocol reconstructs the FILE graph and derives theory edges from it. Neither is a check on the other at the level tested here. 'P3A recall' is therefore NOT computable for this window and was not computed (§42).

p3a_claim: P3A assigns S#### source IDs to every file (F0001=S0028, etc.).
new_finding: This is a THIRD identity system alongside the registry's F#### and the corpus's own source-local labels (C-1, P1, F-1...).
notes: §2 forbids the S-number as a reconstruction UNIT, and §4 forbids a second FILE-ID scheme — but neither says what to do about the S-IDs that already exist. They are useful as a join key into P3A's evidence and should be carried as a cross-reference field, not suppressed and not promoted. Recorded as PILOT-F15.

new_finding: P3A does detect homonyms as a first-class relationship verdict. This is convergent with §19A's identity test and §17's COMPETING_DEFINITION.
notes: Evidence that the two methodologies independently arrived at the need for a same-label-different-concept verdict. Supports §19A's identity test rather than challenging it.

error_mechanism_uniformity: 4 of 4. Every batch-002 disagreement has the identical mechanism, and it is the identical mechanism as all 3 batch-001 disagreements.
prediction: P3A would be wrong for F0011, F0022, F0023, F0024 - predicted from P3A's dates alone, on the hypothesis that a date preceding the file's cluster indicates a cited ruling.
worst_case: F0024 - 38 days of displacement, placing a falsification report five weeks BEFORE the model it falsifies. Corroborated independently by F0020's banner dating the report to 2026-08-02.
agreement_caveat: AGREE is a weaker result than it appears. F0014, F0019 and F0020 all AGREE on value while carrying 2, 2 and 3 typed date events respectively. A scalar that happens to match the earliest event is not evidence that a scalar suffices.
conclusion: P3A's best_historical_date is unsafe as a chronology source in exactly one identifiable circumstance: when a file cites a dated external ruling. That circumstance is COMMON in this corpus (7 of 25) and PREDICTABLE from P3A's own output without reading the file.
